When GST dues outlive the business: what ICAI's updated handbook says about directors, partners, buyers and heirs

When a GST demand cannot be collected from the business, the department looks for someone else to pay it. Sections 85 to 94 of the CGST Act decide who that someone is. ICAI's GST and Indirect Taxes Committee has just released the second edition of its handbook on these provisions, and it is a good prompt to check where your clients stand.

The Handbook on Liability to Pay in Certain Cases under GST, second edition, carries a preface dated October 2026 and states the law as at 30 September 2026. The first edition was published in 2020.

Why this matters now

Recovery has moved from returns to people. As adjudication and appeal backlogs clear, and GSTAT benches decide more cases, confirmed demands against closed, sold or struck-off businesses are turning into notices against directors, partners, buyers of businesses and heirs. Many clients who receive such a notice did not know the liability could follow them.

Transfer of business: section 85

Where a taxable person transfers the business, in whole or in part, by sale, gift, lease, leave and licence, hire or any other manner, the transferor and the transferee are jointly and severally liable for tax, interest and penalty due up to the date of transfer. It does not matter whether the amount was determined before the transfer or afterwards. After the transfer, the transferee is liable for its own supplies and must amend its registration.

The handbook makes a distinction that matters in practice. A transfer of shares alone is not a transfer of business. Buying individual assets is not necessarily a transfer of business either. It cites JR Metal Chennai Ltd v Assistant Commissioner of Central Tax, decided by the Andhra Pradesh High Court on 8 May 2024, where a buyer of plant, land and building argued that it had not taken over the business. The court treated the question as one of fact and sent the party to its appellate remedy. The lesson for any acquirer is that the label on the deed does not settle the question. The substance of what was taken over does.

The handbook also reminds readers that transfer of a going concern, as a whole or an independent part, is exempt under Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28 June 2017, and that Circular 96/15/2019-GST dated 28 March 2019 treats transfer on the death of a sole proprietor as a transfer of ownership for registration and credit purposes.

Amalgamation: section 87

Where companies amalgamate under a court or tribunal order with an earlier appointed date, supplies between them during the interim period are taxable, and the companies are treated as distinct until the date of the order. Their registrations are cancelled from that date. The handbook refers to recent decisions, including Kanakia Spaces Realty v Union of India (Bombay High Court, 24 June 2026), where a notice issued in the name of a company that had ceased to exist on amalgamation was held to be void. The point for practitioners is simple: tell the department about the order, and make sure notices are issued to the right entity.

Liquidation: section 88

A liquidator must inform the Commissioner of the appointment within thirty days. The Commissioner then has three months to tell the liquidator how much should be set aside for tax, interest and penalty. Where a private company is wound up and dues cannot be recovered, every person who was a director during the relevant period is jointly and severally liable, unless the director proves that the failure cannot be attributed to gross neglect, misfeasance or breach of duty. Section 88 operates subject to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.

Directors of private companies: section 89

This is the provision that worries clients most. Notwithstanding the Companies Act, 2013, where dues of a private company for any period cannot be recovered, every person who was a director during that period is jointly and severally liable. The same escape route applies: the director must prove that non-recovery cannot be attributed to gross neglect, misfeasance or breach of duty on his part. If the private company is converted into a public company, the provision does not apply to dues for the private-company period where recovery had already failed, though personal penalties remain recoverable.

Two things follow. The burden is on the director, not the department. And liability turns on who was a director during the period of supply, not who is a director when the notice arrives. A director who resigned in 2021 is not safe for dues of 2019.

Partners: section 90

A firm and each of its partners are jointly and severally liable for the firm's tax, interest and penalty, whatever the partnership deed says. A retiring partner remains liable for dues up to the date of retirement, determined or not. The trap is the intimation. If the partner or the firm does not inform the Commissioner in writing within one month of retirement, the liability continues until the intimation is received. There is no gross-neglect defence for partners.

Death and other cases: section 93

If a business continues after the owner's death, the legal representative or the person carrying it on is liable for dues. If the business is discontinued, the legal representative is liable only to the extent of the estate. Similar rules apply on partition of an HUF or AOP, dissolution of a firm and termination of a guardianship or trust. Each operates subject to the IBC.

The remaining sections cover agents and principals (section 86), guardians, trustees and courts of wards (sections 91 and 92) and certain other cases (section 94). The handbook deals with each.

My reading

Most of these liabilities are avoidable with paperwork done on time. Retiring partners forget the one-month intimation. Buyers of running businesses skip a GST due diligence because the price is attractive. Directors of family private companies sign nothing about compliance and then struggle to show they were not negligent. A liquidator misses the thirty-day intimation and takes on avoidable risk.

The section 89 defence deserves preparation, not improvisation. A non-executive or nominee director should be able to show what was delegated, to whom, what reports were received and what was done when problems surfaced. Board minutes noting GST compliance status, and written delegation to a named officer, are the evidence that later carries the burden.

On acquisitions, I would treat GST exposure like any other contingent liability. Pull the GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and GSTR-9 history, check pending SCNs and orders on the portal, and ask for an indemnity backed by an escrow or retention where the risk is real. Joint and several liability means the department can recover from the buyer first.

Action points

1. For every partner retirement, send a written intimation to the jurisdictional officer within one month and keep the acknowledgement.

2. Run a GST due diligence before buying any running business or business unit: returns, ledgers, notices and pending appeals.

3. Draft business transfer agreements with clear allocation of pre-transfer GST dues, indemnities and a retention or escrow.

4. In private companies, record GST compliance in board minutes and document delegation to a named officer.

5. On amalgamation, file the order with the department promptly and update registrations from the order date.

6. Liquidators must intimate the Commissioner within thirty days of appointment.

7. On a proprietor's death, decide quickly whether the business will continue, because the heir's exposure differs sharply between the two cases.

GST dues do not die with the business. They move to the people who were nearest to it, unless the paperwork was done when it mattered.

This is general information, not advice. Check the provisions and your facts before acting.

Exemption from Liability of Intermediaries in Certain Cases

Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provides legal protection to intermediaries against liability for third-party content hosted or transmitted through their platforms.

An intermediary includes social media platforms, internet service providers, web-hosting companies, search engines, and similar online service providers. Examples include X (Twitter), Facebook, and YouTube.

Sub-section (1)

An intermediary shall not be liable for any third-party information, data, or communication link made available or hosted by it, subject to the conditions specified in the Act.

Sub-section (2)

This protection applies only if:

The intermediary's role is limited to providing access to a communication system through which information is transmitted, temporarily stored, or hosted;

The intermediary does not initiate the transmission;

The intermediary does not select the receiver of the transmission;

The intermediary does not select or modify the information contained in the transmission; and

The intermediary observes due diligence and complies with the requirements prescribed under the Act and the applicable rules.

Sub-section (3)

The protection under Section 79 shall not apply if:

1. The intermediary has conspired, abetted, aided, or induced the commission of an unlawful act; or

2. Upon receiving actual knowledge, or upon being notified by the appropriate Government or its agency that any information, data, or communication link hosted on its computer resource is being used to commit an unlawful act, the intermediary fails to expeditiously remove or disable access to such material while preserving evidence.

Explanation

The term “Third Party Information” refers to any information dealt with by an intermediary in its capacity as an intermediary.

Practical Significance

Section 79 provides a “safe Harbour” to intermediaries. As a result, social media platforms and other intermediaries are generally not automatically liable for content posted by their users. However, if they participate in unlawful activities or fail to act after receiving a valid legal notice or government direction, they may lose the protection granted under Section 79.

The scope of this provision was further clarified by the Supreme Court of India in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India. The Court held that “Actual knowledge” for the purposes of Section 79 generally arises through a court order or a notification issued by a competent government authority, requiring the intermediary to take appropriate action.

INDIA CRACKS DOWN ON AI & DEEP FAKE. BIG TECH PUT ON NOTCE

1. What has actually changed?

The Modi government amended the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 on 10 February 2026 specifically to deal with synthetically generated information and deepfakes.
The framework covers deceptive AI-generated audio, visual and audio-visual material.
The idea is no longer simply: remove illegal content after somebody complains.

Platforms are now being pushed towards:
identification
labelling
metadata
verification
automated detection
rapid takedown
and greater accountability for allowing unlawful AI content to spread.

2. AI CONTENT HAS TO BE IDENTIFIABLE
This is probably the biggest structural change.
AI-generated/synthetically altered material covered by the rules has to be clearly identifiable as synthetic.
Platforms/services enabling generation or alteration of such content must ensure appropriate labels or traceable identifiers/metadata.
The objective is simple:
REAL CONTENT ≠ AI CONTENT
The viewer should not have to conduct a forensic investigation to figure out whether something was artificially generated.
Important nuance

Don't say “every piece of text written using AI anywhere on the internet must carry a label.”

MeitY's FAQ clarifies that the operative 2026 SGI definition primarily targets audio, visual and audio-visual information, not ordinary AI-generated written text.
A more accurate line for your video is:
“India has mandated identification and labelling requirements for covered AI-generated synthetic media, particularly deepfake audio, images and video.”

3. THE BIG NUMBER: 36 HOURS → 3 HOURS

Previously, once an intermediary received legally valid knowledge of unlawful material through the prescribed government/court process, the compliance window could be 36 hours.

That has now been cut to:

3 HOURS

That is a 91.7% reduction in response time.

So something capable of going viral nationally during an election, riot, communal incident, stock-market panic or national-security crisis can no longer theoretically remain online for a day and a half after a valid takedown direction.

The platform has only hours.

4. AND SOME COMPLAINT WINDOWS ARE EVEN SHORTER

The government says timelines for grievance redressal have also been compressed.

According to the PIB explanation:
certain complaints earlier subject to 72 hours can now require action within 36 hours

particularly sensitive categories that earlier had a 24-hour timeline can now require action within 2 hours

This specifically matters for areas such as:

impersonation

intimate imagery

nudity

deepfake abuse

other highly sensitive material.

5. BIG TECH CAN'T JUST WAIT FOR A COMPLAINT

This is another major change.

The government says intermediaries must deploy reasonable and appropriate technical measures, including automated tools or other mechanisms, against unlawful synthetically generated content.
That means platforms are increasingly being pushed from:
REACTIVE MODERATION
to
PROACTIVE DETECTION
For Significant Social Media Intermediaries, the framework explicitly envisages technical measures to identify prohibited content, including certain forms of:

rape-related material

child sexual abuse material

repeat prohibited content

unlawful synthetic content.

6. USERS MAY HAVE TO DECLARE AI CONTENT

The synthetic-media framework also places responsibility upstream.

Major platforms can be required to ask users uploading covered content whether it is synthetically generated and then use technical systems to check that declaration.

So theoretically:
User uploads video →
declares AI/not AI →
platform checks →
synthetic material gets labelled.

The earlier draft framework explicitly envisaged this declaration + technical-verification model.

7. WHY THE METADATA PART MATTERS

A visible watermark can be:

cropped,
blurred,
edited,
screen-recorded,

reposted.

Metadata/identifiers create another layer of traceability.

The government's objective is therefore not merely:

“PUT AI GENERATED IN THE CAPTION.”
It is building a system where synthetic content can carry technological indicators allowing platforms to recognise what it is.
That becomes especially useful once the same manipulated video is downloaded and re-uploaded across multiple platforms.
8. THE RULES TARGET DEEPFAKE IMPERSONATION DIRECTLY
Existing IT Rules already prohibit users from publishing material that:

impersonates another person

misleads users about the origin of a message

knowingly spreads patently false or misleading information

threatens public order

violates another applicable law.

AI does not create an exemption.

If AI is being used for impersonation, fraud, defamatory fabrication or other unlawful activity, existing criminal and cyber provisions can also apply.

9. BNS CAN ALSO COME INTO PLAY
The PIB release specifically points towards provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Depending upon what the deepfake is being used for, authorities could examine provisions relating to:
Section 319 — cheating by personation
Section 336 — forgery

Section 353 — false information/rumours capable of causing public mischief or fear

Section 111 — organised crime, where the factual circumstances justify it.

So there isn't necessarily a standalone offence called simply:

“making a deepfake.”

The legal consequence depends heavily upon what the deepfake does.

10. CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE DEEPFAKES GET SPECIAL ATTENTION
This is perhaps the least discussed but most important provision.
The amended framework explicitly covers harmful AI-generated material involving:
child sexual exploitation

non-consensual intimate imagery

impersonation

other prohibited synthetic material.

Platforms are expected to prevent such content and act rapidly when detected.

11. SOCIAL-MEDIA GIANTS HAVE EXTRA DUTIES

Platforms classified as Significant Social Media Intermediaries, broadly those crossing the prescribed Indian user threshold, face additional compliance obligations.

These include mechanisms involving:
automated detection
grievance officers
compliance officers

local points of contact

India-based compliance structures

periodic compliance reports

appeals processes

originator tracing in specified circumstances for messaging services.
So the rules are aimed not only at the person creating the deepfake.
They put a major compliance burden on the distribution network itself.
12. THE REAL STICK: SAFE HARBOUR
This is where it becomes serious for Meta, X, Google, Telegram and other intermediaries.
Section 79 of the IT Act provides intermediaries conditional protection from liability for third-party content.
But that protection depends upon complying with the law and prescribed due diligence.
The PIB release reiterates that failure to observe obligations under the IT Rules can result in the intermediary losing its Section 79 exemption, after which liability can arise under applicable law.

That makes the real equation:

Comply with due diligence → retain intermediary protection

Ignore statutory obligations → safe-harbour protection can be jeopardised

That is far more powerful than merely issuing a fine.

13. GOVERNMENT HAS BUILT A TAKEDOWN PIPELINE

There is now an increasingly integrated enforcement architecture:

Grievance Appellate Committees — GACs

Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre — I4C

SAHYOG Portal

National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal

police/cybercrime units

authorised State and Central Government agencies.

The SAHYOG system in particular enables centralised electronic communication of lawful content-removal notices to intermediaries.

14. INDIA IS ALSO BUILDING ITS OWN DEEPFAKE-DETECTION TECHNOLOGY

Under the IndiaAI Mission's Safe & Trusted AI pillar, government-backed work includes indigenous detection and governance technologies.
PIB identifies projects including:
Saakshya — multi-agent deepfake-detection framework developed by IIT Jodhpur and IIT Madras
AI Vishleshak — audio-visual forgery detection
IIT Kharagpur work on real-time voice deepfake detection.

So this is not purely a legal crackdown.

It is simultaneously a:

LEGAL + PLATFORM + TECHNOLOGICAL framework.

15. WHY THIS IS HAPPENING NOW

Generative AI has destroyed the old assumption that:
“Seeing is believing.”
Today one person can manufacture:

a politician announcing something he never said

a CEO apparently moving a stock

an Army officer issuing a fake warning

communal speeches

celebrity pornography

fake financial endorsements

fabricated battlefield footage

false evidence of violence
within minutes.
And the fake can reach millions before conventional fact-checking catches up.
Therefore the Indian approach is increasingly:
IDENTIFY → LABEL → DETECT → TRACE → REMOVE → PROSECUTE
rather than merely:
WAIT → RECEIVE COMPLAINT → INVESTIGATE.
THE BIG STORY FOR YOUR VIDEO

The headline isn't simply:

“Deepfakes must carry labels.”

The bigger story is that India is trying to change where responsibility lies.

Earlier, platforms could largely argue:

A user uploaded it; we are merely the intermediary.

The regulatory direction is increasingly:

If you operate the technology that generates, distributes or algorithmically amplifies synthetic content in India, you have duties to identify it, label it and respond rapidly when it becomes unlawful.

This is atrocious, and I need to talk about it.

If you don't know me: I'm a long-time of Nagano-sensei, and I write MAHQ's Five Star Stories section. I want more people to encounter his work. I am a professional translator, though not a JP>EN one.

This is not the first time Titan Comics has done this, of course: people will remember the infamous machine translated / AI slopped release of Kamen Rider Kuuga. They apologised. They said they'd fix it. Then they kept doing it.

Now they have hired an infamous bad actor, well-known in the Grappler Baki and Five Star Stories fan communities. He creates slop translations (with a LOT of slurs!) and tries to sell them. This is the bit I'm in most disbelief about: if there's something Japanese companies are very hardcore about, it is copyright infringement. This is a man who printed bootleg copies of The Five Star Stories with AI slop translations and sold them on ebay. For money.

I cannot imagine that Kadokawa or Nagano-sensei will be happy about this, for starters.

As a fan, of course, it goes beyond copyright infringement and low-quality work. The Five Star Stories might be a niche property outside of Japan, true. In Japan, it is seen as one of the most influential works in the medium, and this year is its 40th anniversary.

It is a dense work, with a lot of complex world-building, science-fantasy terminology, history and politics. It is difficult to translate under ideal conditions. As such, it requires care and quality control.

The fact this is NOT Titan Comics's first time doing this is telling. There is a lack of oversight, and clearly a lack of care for this release. A lack of respect.

In responses to emails from fans, Titan Comics has said they're withdrawing the distribution until they can 'investigate' the matter.

In my opinion, there is only one way to salvage this situation: withdraw the current edition, fire Greco Espinoza, hire a real translator, and then publish it again. They must confirm the translator does not use AI/MTL, and they must do a proper background check on their activities as they should have for Espinoza.

I have been a fan of The Five Star Stories since I picked up a copy of Newtype in 1999. Until Titan Comics fixes this completely, I will be cancelling my much-awaited pre-order.

text:
A reproducible report gives the agent a failing signal and a finish line before it edits code.

“The button does not work” is not a coding-agent task. It is a symptom with the important bits missing. A GitHub issue template can force the report to contain observed behavior, expected behavior, reproduction steps and evidence before an agent turns uncertainty into a confident patch. That tiny structure saves more time than another clever prompt.

Make the template ask for the route or command, environment, exact steps, actual result, expected result and one useful artifact: error text, network response, log or screenshot. Add a field for the acceptance check. If the report says “checkout fails on the second click,” the finish line might be a browser test showing one order after two rapid submissions. “Page opens now” is not enough if the action still duplicates the order.

Give the agent the completed issue and tell it to reproduce the failure before editing. If it cannot reproduce it, it should return the attempted steps and observed result rather than silently fix a guess. Once the failing signal is real, ask for one hypothesis: what code path explains it, what observation would confirm it, and which smallest change would address it? Two failed hypotheses are a reason to inspect new evidence, not to keep changing files randomly.

The regression proof matters. A test that passes on the old behavior does not catch the bug. Ask for the red result before the patch and the green result after it, with exact commands and failures. Pick the cheapest test that crosses the broken boundary: unit for a pure function, integration for an authorization or database path, browser for a visible flow. If the environment cannot run the test, label that as unverified. A generated assertion is not a test result.

Keep the scope in the issue too. A password-reset bug is not permission to redesign authentication. State affected files or modules, non-goals and the condition that should make the agent stop. Ask for a compact final report: root cause, changed files, proof of reproduction, proof of fix and remaining uncertainty. A reviewer should be able to inspect the reasoning without replaying the whole agent conversation.

One honest note: templates are not a substitute for a product decision. If nobody knows the expected behavior, the agent cannot derive it from a screenshot. Route that question to the owner and keep the issue honest. Do not let “works as coded” become the acceptance criterion.

Pick the last bug an agent “fixed” without reproducing it. Turn that missing evidence into a required issue field. Your next repair should start with a fact, not a theory.

America grounded itself: What the 4-hr FAA shutdown really revealed

13 Nov - the United States did something it has done only twice before in its history - it grounded the entire country.

At 3:54 p.m. ET, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop. Every departing flight, at every US airport, was told to stay on the ground. The order was lifted around 8:15-8:30 p.m. ET, after more than 4-hrs.

This was not a weather event nor a security threat but a failure of the system i.e., of the system supposed to keep American aviation in the air.

✲ What happened: The FAA cited 'extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety' after a telecommunications outage hit all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers, the facilities that manage high-altitude, en-route traffic across the country.

Planes already in the air were allowed to continue. International arrivals were handled case-by-case. But departures stopped completely.

By Friday evening, FlightAware had recorded more than 10,000 delays and over 4,000 cancellations. By 8 p.m. ET, cancellations alone had topped 5,000 nationwide, with more than 300 already listed for Sat.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned that recovery would be gradual, and could take days, with priority given to larger aircraft carrying more passengers.

✲ What Mullin said, and why the language mattered: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin was deliberately calm, and deliberately specific:

'There is no prior indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack against us. It is jz a telecommunication outage as of right now.'

'This is not another 9/11. There is no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones.'

'All your loved ones are safe. The public was never in danger through this process.'

'There is no cyberattack.'

He also addressed two anxieties directly - he said he was not aware of the outage impacting other countries, and that he saw 'no reason to connect' the FAA outage to the Microsoft outage reported a day earlier.

Mullin addressed the 9/11 comparison directly because a nationwide ground stop naturally raises security concerns. He said there was no indication of a nefarious attack, that the public was never in danger, and that this was not another 9/11. He later added that the investigation was still open, and that early findings pointed to a technical cause rather than a hostile act.

✲ What caused it: Duffy said instability in radar and communications was first detected at 3:36 p.m. ET at centers and TRACON facilities nationwide.

His diagnosis was blunt - 'what we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system.' Old switches and routers, he said, got 'overloaded' with data and began giving inconsistent readings, forcing the system to be shut down.

Multiple sources told CBS News a more specific trigger - an update to the private communications network that links air traffic control facilities caused the system to reboot and crash. That network is operated by defense contractor L3Harris Technologies. The FAA has not yet confirmed that trigger.

Officials also said there was 'zero evidence' of a cyberattack or rogue AI, and no link to the FAA's new AI tool SMART. Microsoft likewise said it had 'no indication' the ground stop was related to its services.

✲ The most important fact is not what caused the outage, but how little it took to cause it.

America does not have one air traffic control system. It has a patchwork of old analog infrastructure, newer digital layers, and private networks layered on top of each other over decades. When one layer fails, the system does not degrade gracefully, it stops.

This was the third nationwide ground stop in US history, after Sept 11, 2001, and January 2023, when a failure in the pilot notification system grounded flights. The 2001 stop followed a terrorist attack. The 2023 and 2026 stops followed technical failures inside the aviation system, which is why the incident has renewed focus on aging equipment, staffing, and the pace of modernization.

✲ What to watch next is the investigation, the recovery, and the policy response. Investigators still need to confirm what triggered the outage and why it affected all 22 centers. Airlines will need time to reposition aircraft and crews, so delays may continue after flights resume. The incident is also likely to increase discussion about long term investment in air traffic control modernization.

Note: The ground stop has been lifted. Flights are resuming, but schedules remain disrupted. Passengers are advised to check directly with their airline before heading to the airport.

The Centre has issued a notice to messaging platform Telegram, directing it to take concrete measures within 15 days to curb the widespread circulation of pirated films, OTT content and other copyrighted audio-visual material on its platform.

The notice, issued by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B) on July 4, asks Telegram to strengthen its mechanisms for detecting, reporting, disabling access to and removing infringing content. The move is aimed at safeguarding India's creator economy, film industry, broadcasters, OTT platforms, producers and distributors.

The government has also instructed the platform to take action against repeat offenders, including channels, groups, bots, accounts, administrators and associated entities involved in the dissemination of pirated content.

In addition, Telegram has been asked to furnish details of its grievance redressal mechanism available to producers, OTT platforms and law-enforcement agencies, and to submit an Action Taken Report within 15 days outlining the measures implemented to prevent and remove piracy-related material.

The notice signals a shift towards greater platform accountability rather than relying solely on individual takedown requests. The government has previously acted against more than 3,000 Telegram channels allegedly carrying pirated content.

The development comes amid increasing scrutiny of digital platforms over content regulation and compliance. Telegram was also temporarily blocked in India until June 22 in connection with concerns surrounding the NEET-UG re-examination process following allegations of a paper leak and a subsequent investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation.

Illegal Infiltration & Fake Documentation:-A Real Case I Handled

Home Minister @AmitShah ji has held that the population of Muslims in India has increased due to illegal infiltration. Let me share a real case I personally handled about 5–6 years ago in Mumbai, one among many that reveal how deep this problem runs. Please do read to understand the rot.

1. The Client’s Request:- One evening after court hours, a Muslim gentleman known to me came to my office. He had given his premises in Govandi, Mumbai, on a leave and license agreement to a family of 6/7 people.
Even after the agreement expired, the family refused to vacate.

I perused his papers and assured him of appropriate legal action. He then asked if the matter could be resolved sooner than usual.
When I explained that such cases typically take little time, he hesitated and what he said next stunned me.

2. The Shocking Revelation :- He quietly said, “Sir, those tenants are not Indians, they are Bangladeshis.”

That single sentence changed everything. Two thoughts struck me instantly:
1. Why hadn’t he mentioned this earlier?
2. How did they even get valid Aadhaar and PAN cards as visible in the agreement?

3. The Investigation:- On examining the documents, everything looked perfectly legitimate; Aadhaar, PAN, ration card, even voter ID.
We filed RTIs, involved the local police, and began to dig deeper.

Gradually, the truth surfaced, the birth certificate forming the basis of all these documents was forged.

Using that single forged certificate from 1967, the accused had created a full legal identity for himself and his family, including Aadhaar, PAN, ration card, and voter ID.

4. A Web of Fraud:- It didn’t stop there. The man had used the same method to obtain documents for his wife and children. His son was even married to an Indian Muslim woman, effectively merging into the Indian population.

During the investigation, we uncovered an organized network, a full-fledged industry operating to regularize illegal immigrants by manufacturing fake Indian identities that pass every verification test.

5. The Larger Problem:-India’s diversity makes such infiltration even easier. People entering from Bangladesh, Pakistan, Myanmar, or Nepal often resemble locals making visual identification almost impossible.

Add to this the corruption that exists from border checkpoints to administrative offices, and you have a perfect ecosystem for illegal population growth.

In this very case, we found the involvement of certain officials, and shockingly, even a few lawyers.

6. A Moment That Exposed the Rot:- One of those lawyers, representing the Bangladeshi accused, told my Muslim junior,
“How can you do this? This is a matter of religion.”
My junior stood firm and warned him of a complaint before the Bar Council.

This single moment revealed how some individuals, blinded by religious or political motives, are actively protecting those who illegally enter and settle in India.

7. The Unanswered Question:- 
This wasn’t the only case, I have come across several similar ones.
Despite being aware of this menace for years, successive governments have failed to implement a robust national mechanism to identify and deport such individuals.

8. The Hope:- Now that the Home Minister himself has spoken openly about the issue, one can only hope it translates into real, concrete action. India needs a firm, technology-backed, corruption-proof mechanism to detect and remove non-Indians living here on forged documents.

Illegal infiltration is not just a demographic concern, it’s a threat to national integrity, law, and fairness. The time for acknowledgment is over.
The time for action has arrived.

His victims, 31-year-old John Rodriguez and 83-year-old Richard Williams, survived at the scene; however, a few days later, Williams, an Air Force veteran, passed away from his injuries. On March 10, Posada-Hernandez was arrested for attempted murder and had an ICE detainer lodged against him. Prior to this, he had racked up fifteen charges, including domestic violence and aggravated assault. In a press release, ICE revealed that Posada-Hernandez has been deported four different times – most recently in 2020 – and it is unknown when or where he reentered for the fifth time. On March 25, he was indicted on charges of second-degree murder. 
(DHS, March 2026; PIX 11, March 2026; The Hill, March 2026; New York Post, March 2026)

Lopez-Gomez then fled the scene, and Babcock later succumbed to his injuries. Babcock leaves behind a wife, two stepchildren, and a sister. After being located and taken into custody, USCIS confirmed that Lopez-Gomez is an illegal alien who entered the country at an unknown time and place. He remains in custody.

The suspects allegedly set up staged armed robberies, so the store clerks would be able to apply for a U visa. USCIS may grant U visas to “victims of certain crimes who have suffered mental or physical abuse and are helpful to law enforcement or government officials in the investigation or prosecution of criminal activity.” These allow the holder to get a work permit, and, under certain conditions, visa holders may be eligible for permanent residence after a few years. The eleven suspects, all surnamed “Patel”, are accused of allegedly arranging a robbery or paying for themselves or a family member to be a “victim.”

One of the suspects, Rambhai Patel, was previously charged and convicted in New York in December 2023 for conspiracy to commit visa fraud. According to court documents, Rambhai and his co-conspirators set up and carried out staged armed robberies at convenience stores and fast-food restaurants across a few states. All of this was done in front of security cameras, so when the victims called the police, they could offer their help and qualify for a U-visa. The U-Visa Program has been rife with fraud since its inception in 2000, and police agencies have been bombarded with fraudulent applications or reports of fake crimes.

text:
In Constituent Assembly, Mr Tajamul Hussain argued that Muslims should not be given reservation but scheduled caste should be given. The excerpts are enclosed below 

Mr. President, Sir, reservation of seats in any shape or form and for any community or group of people is, in my opinion, absolutely wrong in principle. Therefore I am strongly of opinion that there should be no reservation of seats for anyone and I, as a Muslim, speak for the Muslims. There should be no reservation of seats for the Muslim community. (Hear, Hear). I would like to tell you that in no civilised country where there is parliamentary system on democratic lines, there is any reservation of seats. Take the case of England. The House of Commons is the mother of parliaments. There is no reservation of seats for community there. No doubt they had reservation of seats for the universities but even that has been abolished. What is reservation, Sir? Reservation is nothing but a concession, a safeguard a protection for the weak. We, Muslims do not want any concession. Do not want protection, do not want safeguards. We are not weak. This concession would do more harm than good to the Muslims. Reservation is forcing candidates on unwilling electorates. Whether the electorates wants us or not, we thrust ourselves on them. We do not want to thrust ourselves on unwilling electorates. The majority community will naturally think that we are encroaching upon their rights. We do not want them to think that. We must expert ourselves. Separate electorates have been a curse to India, have done incalculable harm to this country. It was invented by the British. Reservation is the offspring of separate electorates. Do not bring in reservation in the place of separate electorates. Separate electorates have barred our progress. Separate electorates have gone for ever. We desire neither reservation nor separate electorates. We want to merge in the nation. We desire to stand on our own legs. We do not want the support of anyone. We are not weak. We are strong. We are Indians first and we are all Indians and will remain Indians. We shall fight for the honour and glory of India and we shall die for it. (Applause). We shall stand united. There will be no divisions amongst Indians. United we stand; divided we fall. Therefore we do not want reservation. It means division. I ask the members of the majority community who are present here today:-Will you allow us to stand on our legs? Will you allow us to be a part and parcel of the nation? Will you us to be an  equal partner with you? Will you allow us to march shoulder to shoulder with you? Will you allow us to share your sorrows grief and joy? If you do, then for god’s sake keep your hands off reservation for the Muslim community. We do not want statutory safeguard. As I said before, we must stand on our own legs. If we do that, we will have no inferiority complex. We are not inferior to you in any way, Do not make us feel inferior by giving us this concession. I say emphatically there is no difference between you and me. Because we worship the same God by different names, in a different way, that is no reason why we should be considered a minority. We are not a minority. The term ‘minority’ is a British creation. The British created minorities. The British have gone and minorities have gone with them. Remove the term ‘minority’ from your dictionary. (Hear, Hear). There is no minority in India. Only so long as there were separate electorates and reservation of seats there was a majority community and a minority community.

I ask the majority community not to distrust the minorities now. The minorities have adjusted themselves. I will give you a concrete example. You remember the Hyderabad incident; you remember that before you took police action against Hyderabad, what happened. The majority community were afraid that there would be rioting of the Muslims if action was taken against Hyderabad. I was first man to speak about it about a year and half ago in the Central Legislature. I criticised the Government of India. I am sorry Sardar Patel was not present at that time when I was dealing with his portfolio, but my honourable Friend Mr. Gadgil was in charge. I criticised the action of the Government, I told them that they were absolutely mistaken in thinking that the Muslims would rise; they would adjust themselves. I said to them: “You march an army against Hyderabad and within couple of days, you would take the whole of Hyderabad.” I made a long speech and after my speech was over, there was a reply by the Honourable Minister in charge, Mr. Gadgil. He never spoke a single word about it and he never replied to my criticism, but I asked him: “You have replied to everybody’s criticism. Why not mine? I asked you to march an army against Hyderabad; you would take Hyderabad within a couple of days and there would be no rioting.” Mr. Gadgil “You are perfectly right and we will do it.”

I appeal to all minorities to join the majority in creating a secular State. In the new state of things, I want that every citizen in India should be able to rise to the fullest stature and that is why I say that reservation would be suicidal to the minority. I want the minorities to forget that they are minorities in politics. If they think they are minorities in politics, they will be isolated. If they are isolated, the feeling of frustration will cripple them. I do not want to remain minority. Do the minorities, I ask, expect to form part of the great nation and have a hand in the control of its destinies. Can they achieve that aspiration if they are isolated from the rest of India? The minorities if they are returned as minorities, i.e., by reservation of seats can never have an effective voice in the affairs of the country. They can never form a Government. Disraeli could never have formed a Government and could never have become the Prime Minister of England had there been reservation of seats for the Jews in England. I want the minorities to have an honourable place in the Union of India. National interests must always be placed over group interests. The minorities should look forward to the time when they could take their place not under communal or racial labels, but as part and parcel of the whole Indian community.

Now, Sir, with your permission, I want to say a few words with regard to the speeches made against the motion of Sardar Patel. I take first Mr. Muhammad Ismail of Madras. He wants separate electorate. I appeal to his not to ask the charity. Asking for separate electorates is nothing but asking for charity. I tell him that the consequences will be terrible. The majority community will never trust you then. You will never be able to expert yourself. You will be isolated, you will be treated as an alien and your position will be the same as that of the Scheduled Caste. You are not poor. Like the Scheduled Castes, you are not weak, you are not uneducated; you are not uncultured; you can always support yourself. You have produced brilliant men. So do not ask for protection or safeguard. You must have self-confidence in you.  You must expert yourself. You must get into the Assembly by open competition. The times have changed. Adjust yourself. You admitted yesterday in your speech that the atmosphere is better now. I entirely agree with you that the atmosphere is better now. I appeal to you, do not spoil that atmosphere. Improve it, but do not spoil it and if you insist on separate electorate, you will spoil atmosphere very badly. If you get separate electorates, it will again become as bad as before. Say to yourself, Mr. Ismail, that you are an Indian first and an Indian last. Then you will forget all about separate electorates. You will never think of it again.

I will tell you, Sir, that when I had sent in my amendment to clause 292 that it should be deleted, that there should be no reservation of seats, then several Muslim friends to mine, who were for reservation of seats asked me. “Do you realize that the mentality of the Hindus is such at present that if there were no reservation of seats for the Muslims, the Muslims can never succeed?” That honourable gentleman for whom I have got great esteem told me: “Look at us. We have always been with the Congress; we have been to jail and all that. No doubt we will get a ticket from the Congress; many Muslims will get tickets from Socialists and Communists and from other organisations, but what about the electorates? They will never elect you and they will never elect us. So, if there is no reservation, no Muslims will get in because of the mentality of the Hindus.” I told him, Sir, what I am telling you now. I said that I entirely agreed with him that the mentality of the Hindus is such at present. I say to Mr. Ismail also that as long as there is reservation of seats or separate electorate the mentality of the Hindus will never change. You do away with these two things and the mentality will automatically change. I do not want to go into the history of this mentality. I am not going to apportion blame as that will take a long time and you have allotted me a short time and I want to be brief and finish my speech within that time. You all know how the mentality of the Hindus became such, but we have to live in this country, we must change their mentality and it is our duty to change their mentality and the only way the mentality can be changed is to become a part and parcel of the Indian Union. You should say that they are no longer our enemies and then they will be like brothers to us.

Now, Sir, with regard to Mr. Lari, he does not want separate electorates; he does not want reservation of seats; he has condemned both the systems and he says that both the systems are dangerous. He has said that, and I entirely agree with him. He has always opposed separate electorates, reservation of seats and the partition of the country. He is right. But he wants cumulative voting, that is, proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote, or something like that. My honourable Friend, Mr. Saksena has told us that it is a very cumbrous system of mathematical calculations; I am not dealing with that now. The only thing I want to say is that Mr. Lari wants to get into the Assembly by the back door. For example suppose there is a constituency that has to elect four candidates for the House or the People, and there are five candidates. One will be defeated and four will be elected. Out of these five, four are Hindus and one is a Muslim. The votes of the Hindus will be divided among the Hindus and there will get elected. The Muslim will get in on the Muslim votes. Again separate electorates, again reservation of seats. I should like to say to my honourable Friend Mr. Lari if I may say so, that is worse than separate electorate, as the method is not clean. It is not straightforward. I quite understand Mr. Mohamed Ismail’s view when he asks for separate electorates. That is a straightforward method. What is this back-door method of Mr. Lari. I do not understand. I am sure the Muslims do not like these crooked methods; they want a straight, honourable fight. In spite of the fact that Mr. Lari has always openly opposed Pakistan, separate electorates and reservation of seats he still feels inferiority complex. I would ask him to shed this inferiority complex. The country will change for the better.

Last of all, I come to the speech of my honourable and esteemed friend, for whom I have very great regard, Sir Saadulla, the Ex-Premier of Assam. He complains before us that the majority of the Muslim members of the Advisory Committee on Minorities Fundamental Rights etc., did not support the resolution that there should be no reservation of seats for the Muslims. I have already told you, Sir, that I have very great esteem and regard for the Ex-premier of Assam, but I am afraid I must differ from him on this point. I sent my resolution to the Committee to the effect that there should be no reservation of seats. My resolution was discussed under the Chairmanship of the Honourable Sardar Patel. I spoke on my resolution. Begum Aizaz Rasul supported me. Maulana Azad was present there; he did not oppose me. The only person who opposed me was my honourable friend Jafar Imam, from Bihar. There too, I had a majority: Begum Aizaz Rasul. Maulana Azad and myself as against one. The meeting could not be finished and was adjourned sine die. Then it was held on the 11th of this month. I wanted to attend that meeting, particularly because my resolution was there I wanted to move it again. But I never received notice of the meeting. The notice was lying in Delhi; it never reached me. If I had got notice of the meeting. I would have attended it. When I came to Delhi, I learnt that there was the meeting that day. I was happy to learn that the substance of my resolution had been accepted though I was absent. I sent a statement to the Press why I could not attend the meeting that day and it was published in all the papers. Sir Saadulla could not attend the meeting; I do not know why. That meeting was attended by four honourable members: Maulana Azad, Maulana Hifizur Rahman, Begum Aizaz Rasul and Mr. Jaffar Imam. Maulana Azad and Maulana Hifizur Rehman did not oppose my resolution that there should be no reservation of seats.

Every member of this House does not speak. If he oppose, he opposes. If he does not speak, but says “I vote for it“, then he is with it. Maulana Azad was present. If he wanted to oppose, he would have opposed. The two Maulanas did not oppose begum Aizaz Rasul supported my resolution in substance. The resolution was moved by my honourable Friend Dr. Mookherjee. It was the same as my own. Begum Aizaz Rasul supported it. My honourable Friend Mr. Jaffar Imam opposed it. If the Maulana were not with my resolution, they would have sided with Jafar Imam. They said nothing. Votes were taken. There was a clear majority. The Honourable Sardar Patel, I understand, declared that the Muslims were in favour of the motion in spite of the two Maulanas remaining silent. It means that they were with me: three to one voting: there was a majority.

I believe, -I do not remember exactly-there are seven Muslim members on the Committee. Only two are opposed to my resolution; five are with me. The two who are against me are my Hon’ble friends Sir Saadulla and Mr. Jafar Imam. The five who are in favour are , Maulana Azad, Maulana Hifizur Rahman, Begum Aizaz Rasul, Mr. Husseinboy Laljee and myself. Mr. Laljee’s views are well known. He opposed Mr. Jinnah. I know his views. In fact,he wrote to me once, “For God’s sake do something to remove reservations.” Therefore, I had an overwhelming majority. There was another member Syed Ali Zaheer. He is now an Ambassador; I know his views. He is also of the same view as I am.

The next point of my esteemed Friend Sir Saadulla is this. He says, ‘let us take the vote of the Muslim Members here.’ That is a challenge thrown to us. I accept the challenge. I may remind my honourable Friend Sir Saadulla that when the Muslim members came here to Delhi for the first time there was a meeting of all the Muslim members in Western Court. All of them were present. I was the first man to have got up and said that there should be no reservation of seats. I sent my resolution to the Constituent Assembly when you, Sir, were presiding. I regret to say, except one, not a single member supported me. I found that the Muslims wanted reservation. So, I did not move my resolution. That was the first meeting in which the Muslims were against me. The next meeting was in the house of Nawab Muhammad Ismail, about which he also has told you, in 18, Windsor Place. There my view was accepted by an overwhelming majority. The same Muslim members who were present in the Western Court were present here also, and it was passed by an overwhelming majority that there should be no reservation of seats. See how the time had changed. The only member who opposed it was my honourable Friend Sir Saadulla. He is honestly of that opinion; I respect his view. I hope he will respect my view. He said, ‘no there must be reservation of seats‘. But, one thing he said: ‘personally I am not in favour of reservation, but the Muslims want it’. Most humbly I wish to tell him that he is wrong. The Muslims do not want it. Sir Saadulla was the only opposing member. Then there was the Madras group. They are a group by themselves, Sir, I understand their opinion. They have throughout been saying, ” No reservation, but separate electorates; let us have separate electorates.” At the Western Court, they said, “let us have separate electorate,” at Nawab Ismail Sahib’s place also they asked for separate electorates and here also they ask for separate electorates. They are welcome to their opinion. But that there should be no reservation was passed by an overwhelming majority. All of us were present. And after that I sent in my amendment saying that the whole section be deleted or that there should be no reservation for Muslims.

Statement : Meta told the Home Ministry it acted against 61,000 posts in the fortnight after Chalo Sansad. IFF calls for the record to be made public.

New Delhi, 13 November 2026

Meta has told the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), the cybercrime arm of the Ministry of Home Affairs, that it acted on more than 61,000 Facebook and Instagram posts it classified as violent and inciteful between 25 July and 7 August 2026, @ThePrintIndia reported on 12 November. That is about three posts a minute for 14 days. The period begins on the day the Education Minister resigned and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) ended its protest at Jantar Mantar, five days after police used tear gas and a lathi charge against its Chalo Sansad march.

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) condemns the absence of any public account of this action. Meta disclosed the figure to the Home Ministry at a meeting on 21 August, and it became public only because the minutes were filed in the Supreme Court's suo motu proceedings on digital arrest scams.. In IFF's assessment, the minutes record direct pressure from the Ministry of Home Affairs on the content Meta carries.

As per the report in The Print a meeting was chaired by Rajesh Kumar, I4C's chief executive, and followed reviews by the Union Home Secretary, a parliamentary committee and a court-monitored committee on digital arrests. Its scope was wider than financial fraud. 

According to ThePrint, I4C sought an in-person briefing on "how the algorithm amplifies or suppresses specific content and viral accounts", an analysis of bot networks across prominent handles, and Meta's draft guidelines on deepfakes and re-uploaded content for review.
The minutes, as reported, do not state what the 61,000 posts concerned. It is not known which agency, if any, flagged them, or which law or company rule Meta applied. I4C itself did not accept aggregate figures when Meta cited 70 lakh pieces of content removed, it asked for examples with links. Users and the public are entitled to the same detail.

Complaints received by IFF show what was being restricted on Instagram as the period began. Here we are relying on our own inbound queries and requests for pro-bono help and legal assistance.

1) On 23 July, a story about the protests shared by a private account with 137 followers was made unavailable in India through what Instagram described as "an automated system implemented pursuant to legal requirements" under the IT Rules, 2021.

2) On 24 July, a reel by the journalist Ila Kazmi showing a Delhi Police facial recognition van scanning protesters at Jantar Mantar was withheld on a notice from "The Government of India / Law Enforcement under Section 79(3)(b)", which referred her to the Government of India for any questions. The Delhi High Court has directed the Home Ministry, the IT Ministry, the Delhi Police and Meta to produce the notice and will next hear the case on 17 November.

3) On 28 July, three days after the minister's resignation, Instagram withheld a video published on 15 June by the current-affairs page Unmutezone under the title "Why Modi Can't Ask Dharmendra Pradhan to Resign?". Its editor reported that a second video was blocked on 3 August.

Press reports describe similar restrictions. Newslaundry reported that an interview by the journalist Yaqut Ali with a former CJP spokesperson, posted on 26 July, was blocked in India within minutes, and that Facebook reels on the protests by the creator Jyoti Yadav, including an interview with AAP's Sanjay Singh, were restricted. It later reported restrictions on Instagram posts by Scroll and The Hindu about pellet-gun victims in Kashmir. None of this content is violent or inciteful, and Meta has not said whether it forms part of the figure.

The Home Ministry is involved at each stage from notices under Section 79(3)(b) reach platforms through the Sahyog portal, which I4C operates where close to 1.95 lakh blocking orders were issued to Instagram, Facebook and YouTube between March and July 2026, most of them through the portal, and Meta has integrated its systems with it so that flagged content can be restricted without human review. On 27 July the Delhi Police, which reports to the Home Ministry, was reported to have directed platforms to remove posts it considered offensive to the Prime Minister. Meta's transparency report lists violence and incitement among the categories that I4C refers to it. A ministry that operates this channel and also reviews Meta's enforcement figures and algorithm is supervising online speech.

We regret to state that the Supreme Court's own proceedings have provided an avenue for such censorship without sufficient checks and balances. In the suo motu digital arrest case, in which it directed intermediaries to place their proposals before I4C, and in the Just Rights for Children Alliance matters, in which it indicated that platforms may lose safe harbour, the Court has largely acted as a facilitator of executive action rather than as an adjudicator of its constitutional limits. The objectives of curbing fraud and protecting children are legitimate, but the supervision they have enabled now extends to lawful speech and results in censorship without legal authority.

These restrictions do not have a basis in law and often executive rulemaking is being used to circumvent the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression. Section 79(3)(b) sets a condition for a platform's immunity and in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015), the Supreme Court confined it to court orders and government notifications within Article 19(2). The power to block lies in Section 69A, which requires written reasons, committee review and, following Tanul Thakur (2022), a copy of the order and a hearing for the author. Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules requires each intimation to state reasons, the provision, the unlawful act and the URL, and to be reviewed monthly by a Secretary-rank officer. These requirements cannot be met through an automated integration with a three-hour deadline, whatever share of the 61,000 posts came through Sahyog.

Further, we state that while it may constitute a category of harmful speech, "Violent and inciteful" is not a ground for state mandated censorship under Article 19(2). Shreya Singhal protects discussion and advocacy and permits restriction only at the stage of incitement; a video asking why a minister has not resigned is discussion. Nor is there any clear statutory basis for I4C to perform the function of review a platform's content guidelines or to ask which accounts its algorithm promotes.

Our demands

1) The Ministry of Home Affairs must publish the minutes of its meetings with Meta in 2026 and state how many of the 61,000 posts were flagged by I4C, the Delhi Police or any other agency through Sahyog.

2) Meta must publish a breakdown of the 61,000 posts by the rule or law applied, the action taken and the requesting authority, and give each affected user the notice on which it acted. Further monthly breakdowns with qualitative disclosure is necesary.

3) I4C must withdraw its requests to review Meta's draft guidelines and to be briefed on its algorithm. Oversight of this kind requires a law made by Parliament and may only be performed by an independent regulatory body with a clear mandate and objective.

4) The Union Government must publish the monthly Secretary-level reviews under Rule 3(1)(d) for July and August 2026.

5) Meta must end the automatic execution of government and police flags in India and provide human review, a reasoned notice and an opportunity to respond before any restriction.

Users whose posts or accounts were restricted in India in July or August 2026 may write to legal@internetfreedom.in with screenshots of each notice.

text:
Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

This issue may look small, but similar issues are happening everywhere, and no one is noticing them. It feels like “Kare koi aur bhare koi.” Many innocent people face this issue, and it remains unresolved. Because of chain transactions that come into accounts, some people are unable to use their own money. If I travel, I will have to spend more than 6000 rupees to remove the lien. I believe this issue can be resolved through email or online verification, but the investigation officer denied it.

I am also tagging Pushpendra Sir @pushpendrakum and Bangalore Cyber Police @BlrCityPolice . If you could please look into this matter.

Thank you.

👮‍♂️ “Let me see some ID. Otherwise, you’re going to have to leave the property. It’s government property. I can make you leave.” - about a public parking lot.

During a First Amendment audit at the Harford County Government Administrative Offices in Bel Air, MD, Long Island Audit (SeanPaul Reyes) was recording in a publicly accessible parking area.

HCSO Deputy B.F. Chandler demanded ID, threatened to remove him from the property, initially refused to identify himself, and covered his name tag with his arm before calling for backup over the filming of public vehicle tags.

HCSO backup Deputies Colson and Davis arrived, identified themselves, and did not escalate. 

Bel Air Police Officer Green confirmed there is no law against filming in the public lot.

No arrest or charges. 

Reyes rated the audit a fail for Deputy Chandler (unprofessional and unaware of rights/policy) and a pass for the others who recognized the activity as legal. 

HCSO Policy ADM 1203, now affirms the First Amendment right to record in public as long as it does not create a safety threat. 

Sheriff Jeff Gahler has publicly acknowledged recording rights under his leadership.

❓Backup deputies shrugged it off — so why did the first deputy escalate over photography?

❓Why did the first deputy cover his name tag when asked to identify himself?

India Arrests Suspect Deported from Sri Lanka in Human Trafficking Case.

India’s National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested Pudumadam Imran at Bengaluru Airport on Friday (Nov. 13) after Sri Lankan authorities repatriated him following an INTERPOL Red Notice. 

NIA Press Release 👇🏻 

NIA ARRESTS DEPORTED ACCUSED IN SRI LANKA HUMAN TRAFFICKING CASE

Bengaluru, 13th November 2026

The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has today arrested accused Pudumadam Imran (A-15), who had evaded arrest and was absconding in the Sri Lanka human trafficking case, from Bengaluru International Airport. He had been detained on the basis of a Red Notice issued by INTERPOL at the request of NIA, and was repatriated to India by the Sri Lankan authorities, following which he was arrested by NIA.

The accused actively participated in the conspiracy to traffic the victims from Sri Lanka with the false promise of taking them to Canada with valid documents, for which he collected money from their family members or relatives. He sent money through hawala channels to co-accused persons in India for the trafficking and confinement of the victims.

The case pertains to raids conducted by local Police at premises in Mangalore, based on credible information, uncovering Sri Lankan citizens without valid documents. A case was registered vide Cr. No. 103/2021 under various sections of the IPC, the Foreigners’ Act and the Passport Act. Subsequently, on 13th July 2021, NIA re-registered the case as RC-17/2021/NIA/DLI under sections 120B, 370 and 420 of the IPC, section 14 of the Foreigners’ Act and section 12(1A) of the Passport Act.

Earlier in the case, 2 absconding accused, Seeni Aabul Khan (A-9) and Imran Khan (A-7), were arrested in 2024 and 2025, respectively, and are currently facing trial before the Special Court for Trial of NIA Cases, Bengaluru.

PUBLIC STATEMENT BY PARANJOY GUHA THAKURTA
On the arbitrary takedown of https://t.co/TMPhYqaVhe by Hostinger following legal notices from Indiabulls founder Sameer Gehlaut
October 31, 2026
On the morning of October 28, 2026, my website https://t.co/OeAAoTPXCy and all its associated subdomains, including https://t.co/I8kylhDXVk and https://t.co/D8b6LtNzWD, were abruptly taken offline by our web hosting provider, Hostinger (HOSTINGER operations, UAB). The website, registered twelve years ago, serves as an online archive of my work over several decades as a journalist, author, publisher, and maker of documentary films and music videos
Hostinger gave no prior intimation, warning, or opportunity to respond before suspending the entire hosting account. When my colleague contacted Hostinger “Support” at 6:48 AM on October 28, a hosting “specialist” stated that the suspension was triggered by an abuse report for "Fraud/Scam" and declared that "unsuspension is not negotiable in this case."
This sudden shutdown of an entire repository under the label "Fraud/Scam" happened just days after Sameer Gehlaut, founder of the Indiabulls group, served me with an ex parte court order demanding the removal of a single article published more than seven years on https://t.co/25noyNupwJ.
For over six years, Indiabulls and Shri Gehlaut have pursued legal action over this report and I have consistently defended our journalistic report in court. Here is the timeline:
·  March 11, 2020: Indiabulls Housing Finance Limited filed a criminal defamation complaint (CC No. 1765/2020) before the Patiala House Courts, New Delhi, against NewsClick, its Reader's Editor Urmilesh, co-author of the article Sourodipto Sanyal, NewsClick editor Prabir Purkayastha, and me over an article published on the website on September 30, 2019.
·  June 6, 2025 and July 9, 2025: More than five years after the complaint was filed, a Judicial Magistrate at Patiala House Courts passed an order on June 6, 2025, dropping proceedings against Shri Purkayastha while issuing summons to the remaining four accused, including me, under Sections 499 and 500 of the Indian Penal Code. A formal summons was issued on July 9, 2025, for appearance on July 30, 2025.
·  August 27, 2026: Counsel for Shri Gehlaut, sent me a legal notice demanding the takedown of the article within 24 to 48 hours, claiming that a status report by the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of the Delhi Police had altered the factual position.
·  September 2, 2026: My counsel sent a reply pointing out concerns with the legal notice
·  October 24, 2026: Indiabulls Nests Limited (Plaintiff No. 1) and Sameer Gehlaut (Plaintiff No. 2) obtained an ex parte ad interim injunction from the Court of one of the District and Sessions Judges, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi, in Civil Suit No. 529/2026 (Indiabulls Nests Ltd. & Anr. v. Ashok Kumar/John Doe & Ors.), in which I am arrayed as Defendant No. 19. The order directed the removal and de-indexing of the article on https://t.co/TMPhYqaVhe (listed as Item A-33 in Schedule A).
·  October 25, 2026 (10:13 AM IST): Advocates representing Indiabulls Nests Limited and Sameer Gehlaut, emailed me the October 24 court order and suit documents, demanding immediate deletion and written confirmation of compliance.
·  October 26, 2026 (11:33 PM IST): Sameer Gehlaut personally sent an email from his official address (sameer@indiabulls.com) demanding the immediate deletion of the URL from https://t.co/TMPhYqaVhe and threatening to move the court under Order XXXIX Rule 2A of the Code of Civil Procedure if I did not comply, noting that the matter is next listed on December 18, 2026. While I was in the process of challenging the order dated 24.10.2026 before higher forums, on the same day, advocates representing Shri Gehlaut submitted a court order takedown complaint to Google LLC.

·  October 28, 2026 (3:16 PM IST): Google Search Console sent an automated notice ([WNC-598900]) informing me that Google was blocking the specific URL https://t.co/SsSVUVLKGX  from appearing in search results on https://t.co/2IOZ4I1WqC.

The Lumen Database record of this complaint (Notice ID: 101001876) reveals the scale of the takedown request. The complaint targeted 52 URLs on websites across major national and international news organisations, including The Economic Times, Business Standard, The Caravan, The Daily Pioneer, Business Today, Deccan Herald, ET Now, Financial Express, Livemint, Moneycontrol, Moneylife, NDTV Profit, The New Indian Express, Outlook Business, The Quint, Quartz, and NewsClick, along with posts on X (formerly Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and Scribd.

Most of these reports on major corporate news websites remain accessible online. In fact, Item 39 on the Lumen takedown list is the original September 30, 2019 article published on https://t.co/qQP2N2fxA2: https://t.co/hgneAPvDuF, which remains live and accessible  as of now.

Yet, in the case of https://t.co/TMPhYqaVhe, the entire domain and every website hosted on my account were wiped off the internet.

Hostinger's Baseless "Fraud/Scam" Claim and Demand for Accountability

Hostinger did not cite the Patiala House Courts order when it suspended my account on October 28, 2026. Instead, its representative claimed that the hosting account was permanently suspended due to an abuse report for "Fraud/Scam".

This allegation is demonstrably false:

1. VirusTotal Security Analysis: Independent domain checks conducted on October 28, 2026, at 7:48 AM and 7:54 AM on VirusTotal confirm that 0 out of 92 security vendors flagged https://t.co/TMPhYqaVhe or https://t.co/I8kylhDXVk as malicious, phishing, or fraudulent. VirusTotal explicitly categorises https://t.co/TMPhYqaVhe under "news and media".

2. Google Safe Browsing Status: Checks on the Google Safe Browsing diagnostic tool at 7:55 AM and 7:56 AM on October 28, 2026, for both https://t.co/TMPhYqaVhe and https://t.co/D8b6LtNzWD returned the status: "No unsafe content found".
My website https://t.co/OeAAoTPXCy does not sell financial products, solicit funds for commercial schemes, or engage in any activity that could remotely be classified as a scam. It is a repository of public-interest journalism, books, documentary films, and investigative reports built over a lifetime of work. By acting on a fabricated "Fraud/Scam" abuse report without a single verification check or prior notice to the domain owner, Hostinger has allowed its abuse-reporting mechanism to be weaponised to censor an independent journalist.
Even where a court order directs the removal or de-indexing of a specific URL, a web hosting provider has no legal or ethical justification to pull down an entire domain and hundreds of unrelated articles, archives, and subdomains without notice.
I demand immediate answers and accountability from Hostinger:
1. Who submitted the false "Fraud/Scam" abuse report against https://t.co/TMPhYqaVhe, and on what exact date and time was it received?
2. What internal verification did Hostinger's abuse team conduct before classifying a 12-year-old journalism portal as a "Fraud/Scam" site, especially when 92 security vendors on VirusTotal and Google Safe Browsing show zero malicious or unsafe content?
3. Why was no prior notice, warning, or copy of the complaint sent to me before suspending the entire hosting account?
4. On what basis did Hostinger's specialist declare that the suspension of an entire archive of journalistic work is "not negotiable"?
While my legal advisers are in the process of taking appropriate steps in court regarding the ex parte order dated October 24, 2026, and the wholesale suspension of my website, this backdoor censorship through web hosting providers sets a dangerous precedent for the independence of the media and freedom of expression as enshrined in Article (19)(1)(a) of the Constitution of India as a fundamental right of every citizen of India.
Yours sincerely

Paranjoy Guha Thakurta
Independent Journalist, Author, Publisher and Maker of Documentary Films and Music Videos
